title: Explain Concepts Related to Integration of Systems

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: Modern cloud environments contain many different services, applications, and platforms. Those systems need ways to communicate.
CompTIA wants you to recognize event-driven architectures, REST, SOAP, RPC, WebSockets, and GraphQL.
The key mental model is: How are these systems exchanging information?

sections.title: Maestro Focus
paragraphs: Is communication triggered by an event, based on web requests, calling a remote function, maintaining a live connection, or requesting specific data?

sections.title: Event-Driven Architectures
paragraphs: An event-driven architecture reacts when events occur, such as a file upload, completed purchase, created user, or received message.
Instead of constantly asking whether something changed, a component can react when the event happens.
Think: Something happened → do something.
sections.callout: An action occurs automatically because another event happened → event-driven architecture.

sections.title: Web Services
paragraphs: Web services allow systems to communicate over networks using defined interfaces. CompTIA focuses on three approaches: REST, SOAP, and RPC.

entries.title: Representational State Transfer (REST)
paragraphs: REST is a common approach for building web APIs and commonly works with resources using familiar web operations.
Conceptual operations include retrieving, creating, modifying, and deleting information.
Think: Web-style API communication around resources.
entries.recognitionCue: Applications interact through a lightweight web API based around resources → REST.

entries.title: Simple Object Access Protocol (SOAP)
paragraphs: SOAP is a structured web-service protocol that commonly uses XML-formatted messages. It is more formal and structured than many REST-style services.
Think: Structured XML-based web-service communication.
entries.recognitionCue: Formal web-service messaging uses XML → SOAP.

entries.title: Remote Procedure Call (RPC)
paragraphs: RPC allows one system to request that a procedure or function execute on another system.
To the developer, it can resemble calling a function even though the function executes remotely.
Think: Run this function over there.
entries.recognitionCue: One system invokes a procedure on another system → RPC.

table.caption: REST, SOAP, and RPC comparison
rows: Invoke a remote function or procedure

sections.title: WebSockets
paragraphs: WebSockets provide a persistent two-way communication channel between systems.
Unlike a one-time request and response, a WebSocket connection can remain open so both sides continue sending information.
Good recognition scenarios include live updates, real-time messaging, and interactive applications.
Think: Keep the communication line open.
sections.callout: Client and server need continuous real-time two-way communication → WebSockets.

sections.title: GraphQL
paragraphs: GraphQL allows a client to request the specific data fields it needs.
Instead of receiving a fixed response containing unnecessary information, the client describes the data it wants.
Think: Give me exactly these fields.
sections.callout: The client needs to request precisely selected data from an API → GraphQL.

sections.title: Recognition Cues
bullets: Event causes automatic action → Event-driven architecture
Execute a function on a remote system → RPC
Client specifies exactly which fields it wants → GraphQL

entries.title: REST vs. SOAP
paragraphs: Both can integrate systems through web services. REST is lightweight and resource-oriented. SOAP uses a structured protocol and XML.

entries.title: REST vs. GraphQL
paragraphs: REST commonly exposes defined resources and endpoints. GraphQL lets the client specify exactly which data it wants.

entries.title: RPC vs. REST
paragraphs: RPC thinks in terms of performing a procedure. REST thinks in terms of interacting with a resource.

entries.title: WebSockets vs. Normal Request/Response
paragraphs: If communication must remain open for real-time interaction, choose WebSockets.

sections.title: Maestro Recognition Sheet
bullets: React when an event occurs → Event-driven architecture
Give me only these fields → GraphQL
